format:

    fontsize: 9pt
    margin:
      top: 2.1cm
      bottom: 1.9cm
      left: 1.7cm
      right: 1.7cm
    mainfont: "Segoe UI"
    section-numbering: ""
brand:
  color:
    palette:
      paper: "#FFFFFF"
      ink: "#22282E"
      ink-soft: "#5C666F"
      red: "#C10016"
      blue: "#0F4C81"
    background: paper
    foreground: ink
    primary: blue

  # No font is named beyond the one above, so nothing is fetched from a font
  # service; a system without it falls back to the default of the renderer.
  typography:
    headings:
      weight: bold
      color: red
knitr:
  opts_chunk:
    echo: false
    message: false
    warning: false
    dev: "ragg_png"
    dev.args: {bg: "white"}
    dpi: 300
    fig-width: 6.8
    fig-height: 2.5
execute:
  error: true
---

```{r setup}
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# What to set for an issuer
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# The path to the config file, whose esef section names the Silver layer of
# the module. A chunk runs with the directory of this template as its working
# directory, which is inside the installed package, so the path is taken from
# the environment variable FINCOMMONS_CONFIG where it is set and is otherwise
# a paths.yaml beside the template.
config_path <- Sys.getenv("FINCOMMONS_CONFIG", "paths.yaml")

# The issuer, by its LEI. This is voestalpine AG; any other issuer whose
# country the esef pipeline has collected can be put here.
lei <- "529900ZAXBMQDIWPNB72"

# The number of financial years shown, counted back from the latest filing.
# One further year is read behind them, because a return puts a flow of a
# year against the average of the balances at its start and its end, and
# because the screening indicators compare a year with the one before it.
n_years <- 6

# Amounts are shown in millions of the currency of the report.
scale <- 1e6

# The point size of the text in a chart. A chart stands in a page of nine
# point text, so it is set a little smaller than the page around it.
chart_base_size <- 9

# You can change the language of the figures here, but they must be
# implemented for each figure separately by you. The language also picks the
# filing: an issuer that files its report in English and in German has two
# filings per year with the same figures, and the texts are taken from the
# one in the language of the factsheet where there is one. voestalpine has
# filed in German only since its report for 2021/22, so its texts are German
# whatever the language set here.
lang <- "en"

# The month names in the captions come from the system locale rather than
# from the language set above, so the locale for dates is set from lang.
invisible(Sys.setlocale("LC_TIME", if (lang == "de") "German" else "C"))

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The concepts the factsheet is built from
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Only concepts of the IFRS taxonomy are used here. An issuer may tag a line
# of its statements with a concept of its own instead, but an extension
# concept is the issuer's to name and rename from one year to the next, so
# the ones this factsheet needs are kept apart in `extension_concepts`
# below. A figure that is in neither list is derived from those that are, in
# the next chunk, or left out.
#
# The key is what the code below refers to, so a concept can be swapped for
# another issuer's presentation without touching the figures. A key may be
# given more than one concept, in order of preference, for an issuer that
# changed the tag of a line: voestalpine tags its property, plant and
# equipment as PropertyPlantAndEquipment up to 2024/25 and with the
# right-of-use assets in the concept's name since.
#
# Expenses, including tax, are tagged as positive amounts by the taxonomy
# and stand in the tables as the deductions they are; see `sign` in the
# lines of the statements further down.
concepts <- c(
  # Statement of financial position: assets
  assets = "ifrs-full:Assets",
  noncurrent_assets = "ifrs-full:NoncurrentAssets",
  ppe = "ifrs-full:PropertyPlantAndEquipmentIncludingRightofuseAssets",
  ppe = "ifrs-full:PropertyPlantAndEquipment",
  goodwill = "ifrs-full:Goodwill",
  intangibles = "ifrs-full:IntangibleAssetsOtherThanGoodwill",
  equity_method = "ifrs-full:InvestmentAccountedForUsingEquityMethod",
  financial_assets_noncurrent = "ifrs-full:OtherNoncurrentFinancialAssets",
  deferred_tax_assets = "ifrs-full:DeferredTaxAssets",
  current_assets = "ifrs-full:CurrentAssets",
  inventories = "ifrs-full:Inventories",
  receivables = "ifrs-full:TradeAndOtherCurrentReceivables",
  financial_assets_current = "ifrs-full:OtherCurrentFinancialAssets",
  cash = "ifrs-full:CashAndCashEquivalents",

  # Statement of financial position: equity and liabilities
  equity_and_liabilities = "ifrs-full:EquityAndLiabilities",
  equity = "ifrs-full:Equity",
  equity_owners = "ifrs-full:EquityAttributableToOwnersOfParent",
  issued_capital = "ifrs-full:IssuedCapital",
  additional_paid_in = "ifrs-full:AdditionalPaidinCapital",
  retained_earnings = "ifrs-full:RetainedEarnings",
  other_reserves = "ifrs-full:OtherReserves",
  treasury_shares = "ifrs-full:TreasuryShares",
  nci = "ifrs-full:NoncontrollingInterests",
  noncurrent_liabilities = "ifrs-full:NoncurrentLiabilities",
  financial_liabilities_noncurrent = "ifrs-full:OtherNoncurrentFinancialLiabilities",
  employee_provisions = "ifrs-full:NoncurrentProvisionsForEmployeeBenefits",
  deferred_tax_liabilities = "ifrs-full:DeferredTaxLiabilities",
  current_liabilities = "ifrs-full:CurrentLiabilities",
  financial_liabilities_current = "ifrs-full:OtherCurrentFinancialLiabilities",
  payables = "ifrs-full:TradeAndOtherCurrentPayables",
  current_provisions = "ifrs-full:CurrentProvisions",
  current_tax_liabilities = "ifrs-full:CurrentTaxLiabilitiesCurrent",

  # Statement of profit or loss
  revenue = "ifrs-full:Revenue",
  cost_of_sales = "ifrs-full:CostOfSales",
  gross_profit = "ifrs-full:GrossProfit",
  distribution_costs = "ifrs-full:DistributionCosts",
  admin_expense = "ifrs-full:AdministrativeExpense",
  other_income = "ifrs-full:OtherIncome",
  other_expense = "ifrs-full:OtherExpenseByFunction",
  associates_result = "ifrs-full:ShareOfProfitLossOfAssociatesAndJointVenturesAccountedForUsingEquityMethod",
  ebit = "ifrs-full:ProfitLossFromOperatingActivities",
  finance_income = "ifrs-full:FinanceIncome",
  finance_costs = "ifrs-full:FinanceCosts",
  profit_before_tax = "ifrs-full:ProfitLossBeforeTax",
  income_tax = "ifrs-full:IncomeTaxExpenseContinuingOperations",
  profit_continuing = "ifrs-full:ProfitLossFromContinuingOperations",
  profit_discontinued = "ifrs-full:ProfitLossFromDiscontinuedOperations",
  profit = "ifrs-full:ProfitLoss",
  profit_owners = "ifrs-full:ProfitLossAttributableToOwnersOfParent",
  profit_nci = "ifrs-full:ProfitLossAttributableToNoncontrollingInterests",

  # Other comprehensive income
  oci = "ifrs-full:OtherComprehensiveIncome",
  oci_translation = "ifrs-full:OtherComprehensiveIncomeNetOfTaxExchangeDifferencesOnTranslation",
  oci_hedges = "ifrs-full:OtherComprehensiveIncomeNetOfTaxCashFlowHedges",
  oci_reclassified = "ifrs-full:OtherComprehensiveIncomeThatWillBeReclassifiedToProfitOrLossNetOfTax",
  oci_not_reclassified = "ifrs-full:OtherComprehensiveIncomeThatWillNotBeReclassifiedToProfitOrLossNetOfTax",
  comprehensive_income = "ifrs-full:ComprehensiveIncome",
  comprehensive_income_owners = "ifrs-full:ComprehensiveIncomeAttributableToOwnersOfParent",

  # Per share
  eps = "ifrs-full:BasicEarningsLossPerShare",
  eps = "ifrs-full:BasicAndDilutedEarningsLossPerShare",
  eps_diluted = "ifrs-full:DilutedEarningsLossPerShare",
  eps_diluted = "ifrs-full:BasicAndDilutedEarningsLossPerShare",
  dps = "ifrs-full:DividendsProposedOrDeclaredBeforeFinancialStatementsAuthorisedForIssueButNotRecognisedAsDistributionToOwnersPerShare",

  # Statement of cash flows
  operating_cash_flow = "ifrs-full:CashFlowsFromUsedInOperatingActivities",
  investing_cash_flow = "ifrs-full:CashFlowsFromUsedInInvestingActivities",
  financing_cash_flow = "ifrs-full:CashFlowsFromUsedInFinancingActivities",
  cash_change = "ifrs-full:IncreaseDecreaseInCashAndCashEquivalentsBeforeEffectOfExchangeRateChanges",
  fx_on_cash = "ifrs-full:EffectOfExchangeRateChangesOnCashAndCashEquivalents",
  interest_paid = "ifrs-full:InterestPaidClassifiedAsOperatingActivities",
  interest_received = "ifrs-full:InterestReceivedClassifiedAsOperatingActivities",
  taxes_paid = "ifrs-full:IncomeTaxesPaidRefundClassifiedAsOperatingActivities",
  dividends_received = "ifrs-full:DividendsReceivedClassifiedAsOperatingActivities",
  acquisitions = "ifrs-full:CashFlowsUsedInObtainingControlOfSubsidiariesOrOtherBusinessesClassifiedAsInvestingActivities",
  disposals_of_businesses = "ifrs-full:CashFlowsFromLosingControlOfSubsidiariesOrOtherBusinessesClassifiedAsInvestingActivities",
  proceeds_borrowings = "ifrs-full:ProceedsFromBorrowingsClassifiedAsFinancingActivities",
  repayments_borrowings = "ifrs-full:RepaymentsOfBorrowingsClassifiedAsFinancingActivities",
  lease_payments = "ifrs-full:PaymentsOfLeaseLiabilitiesClassifiedAsFinancingActivities",
  buybacks = "ifrs-full:PaymentsToAcquireOrRedeemEntitysShares",
  dividends_paid = "ifrs-full:DividendsPaid",
  dividends_paid_nci = "ifrs-full:DividendsPaidToNoncontrollingInterestsClassifiedAsFinancingActivities"
)

# The concepts of the issuer's own taxonomy that the factsheet uses, with the
# same keys as above. These are the lines an issuer presents that the IFRS
# taxonomy has no concept for, and they are the first thing to look at when
# the factsheet is pointed at another issuer: the names are the issuer's own,
# in the issuer's own language, and it may rename them from one year to the
# next. Every figure that rests on one carries a mark in the tables, and the
# page on the coverage of the tags reports how many years each was found in.
#
# voestalpine presents its capital expenditure, its proceeds from disposals
# and the movement in its working capital in its cash flow statement under
# concepts of its own, and tagged its earnings per share for 2021/22 that
# way as well.
extension_concepts <- c(
  capex = "voestalpineag:InvestitionenInAndereImmaterielleVermoegenswerteUndSachanlagen",
  asset_disposals = "voestalpineag:EinnahmenAusDemAbgangVonAnlagevermoegen",
  financial_investments = "voestalpineag:InvestitionenDevestitionenInAndereFinanzanlagen",
  working_capital_change = "voestalpineag:VeraenderungWorkingCapital",
  noncash_items = "voestalpineag:NichtZahlungswirksameAufwendungenUndErtraege",
  eps = "voestalpineag:VerwaessertesUndUnverwaessertesErgebnisJeAktieEUR",
  eps_diluted = "voestalpineag:VerwaessertesUndUnverwaessertesErgebnisJeAktieEUR"
)

# The texts of the report shown in the profile of the issuer.
text_concepts <- c(
  name = "ifrs-full:NameOfReportingEntityOrOtherMeansOfIdentification",
  legal_form = "ifrs-full:LegalFormOfEntity",
  domicile = "ifrs-full:DomicileOfEntity",
  country_of_incorporation = "ifrs-full:CountryOfIncorporation",
  address = "ifrs-full:AddressOfRegisteredOfficeOfEntity",
  principal_place = "ifrs-full:PrincipalPlaceOfBusiness",
  parent = "ifrs-full:NameOfUltimateParentOfGroup",
  activities = "ifrs-full:DescriptionOfNatureOfEntitysOperationsAndPrincipalActivities",
  period_covered = "ifrs-full:PeriodCoveredByFinancialStatements",
  statements_basis = "ifrs-full:DescriptionOfPresentationCurrency"
)

# You can adapt your corporate design in the sourced R-Skript
library(ggplot2)
source("r-corporate-design-functions-ggplot2.R")

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(yaml)
library(arrow)

# The label of a financial year. A year that ends on 31 December is named by
# its calendar year, and any other by the two it spans, as voestalpine's
# financial year from April to March is: 2025/26 ends on 31 March 2026.
fy_label <- function(date) {
  y <- as.integer(format(date, "%Y"))
  ifelse(format(date, "%m-%d") == "12-31", as.character(y),
         paste0(y - 1, "/", sprintf("%02d", y %% 100)))
}

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The Silver layer
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

yaml_paths <- read_yaml(config_path)
path_silver <- yaml_paths[["esef"]][["silver"]]

# The Silver layer may name a schema in a catalogue rather than a directory,
# with the directory the tables are written to beside it. R reads files, so
# it takes the directory.
if (is.list(path_silver)) path_silver <- path_silver[["path"]]

# arrow reads every parquet file under a directory. A Delta table keeps the
# files it has replaced until it is vacuumed, and the table of facts replaces
# a country's partition on every run that finds new reports, so a Delta table
# read this way counts a fact once for every time it was written. The
# factsheet therefore refuses one rather than show those sums.
for (table in c("filings", "facts")) {
  if (dir.exists(file.path(path_silver, table, "_delta_log"))) {
    stop("The ", table, " table of the esef module is a Delta table, which ",
         "this template does not read. Write the Silver layer as parquet, ",
         "or read the table through Spark.")
  }
}

filings_all <- open_dataset(file.path(path_silver, "filings")) %>%
  filter(LEI == lei) %>%
  collect()

if (nrow(filings_all) == 0) {
  stop("The table of filings lists no filing of ", lei, ". The table lists ",
       "every country, so the LEI is likely wrong.")
}

# One filing per financial year. A report filed in two languages, or filed
# again with corrections, is a filing of its own with facts of its own, and
# the figures of the year are taken from one of them: the one in the
# language of the factsheet, then the one with fewer validation errors, then
# the one the repository processed last. A filing without a JSONURL has no
# facts and is never chosen while another one is there.
filings <- filings_all %>%
  arrange(PERIODEND,
          is.na(JSONURL),
          coalesce(LANG, "") != lang,
          coalesce(ERRORS, 0L),
          desc(PROCESSED)) %>%
  group_by(PERIODEND) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(!is.na(JSONURL)) %>%
  arrange(PERIODEND) %>%
  slice_tail(n = n_years + 1)

if (nrow(filings) == 0) {
  stop("No filing of ", lei, " has facts in the Silver layer. Run the esef ",
       "pipeline for the issuer's country first.")
}

latest <- filings %>% slice_tail(n = 1)
issuer_name <- latest$NAME

facts <- open_dataset(file.path(path_silver, "facts")) %>%
  filter(LEI == lei, FILING %in% filings$FILING) %>%
  collect()

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The figures, one row per financial year
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# The figures of a year are the totals the year's own filing reports for the
# year: no dimensions, a period that ends on the period end of the filing,
# and, for a flow, a period that begins a year before it. The comparative
# figures of the previous year that every filing carries as well are left
# aside, so that a restated figure does not stand beside the one first
# reported without saying so. The same fact may be tagged more than once in
# a report, in the statements and again in the notes, with the same value.
figures <- facts %>%
  filter(is.na(DIMENSIONS), !is.na(VALUE), PRDEND == PERIODEND,
         is.na(PRDSTART) | PRDSTART == PERIODEND - 364 |
           PRDSTART == PERIODEND - 365) %>%
  distinct(PERIODEND, CONCEPT, UNIT, VALUE) %>%
  group_by(PERIODEND, CONCEPT) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  ungroup()

currency <- figures %>%
  filter(CONCEPT == concepts[["assets"]]) %>%
  slice_tail(n = 1) %>%
  pull("UNIT") %>%
  sub("^iso4217:", "", x = .)
if (length(currency) == 0) currency <- ""

# One row per year, one column per key of the concepts above, from the first
# of a key's concepts the year's filing tags. The concepts of the taxonomy
# come first and the issuer's own after them, so that a line tagged both ways
# is taken from the taxonomy. A concept the issuer did not tag at all stays a
# column of missing values, so that the figures below show a gap rather than
# fail.
keys_all <- c(names(concepts), names(extension_concepts))
lookup <- bind_rows(
  tibble(key = names(concepts), CONCEPT = unname(concepts),
         preference = seq_along(concepts), extension = FALSE),
  tibble(key = names(extension_concepts), CONCEPT = unname(extension_concepts),
         preference = length(concepts) + seq_along(extension_concepts),
         extension = TRUE))

tagged <- figures %>%
  inner_join(lookup, by = "CONCEPT") %>%
  group_by(PERIODEND, key) %>%
  slice_min(preference, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup()

wide <- tagged %>%
  select(PERIODEND, key, VALUE) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = "key", values_from = "VALUE") %>%
  arrange(PERIODEND)
for (key in setdiff(unique(keys_all), names(wide))) {
  wide[[key]] <- NA_real_
}

# Which keys were read from a concept of the issuer's own taxonomy, and in
# how many of the years shown. The tables mark a line that rests on one, and
# the page on the coverage of the tags lists them.
extension_used <- tagged %>%
  filter(extension) %>%
  count(key, CONCEPT, name = "years")
is_extension <- function(key) key %in% extension_used$key

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The figures the statements do not carry under a concept of their own
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# voestalpine presents its income statement by function: revenue less cost
# of sales is gross profit, and gross profit less distribution and
# administrative costs, plus other operating income less other operating
# expenses and the result of its associates, is the operating result, which
# it calls EBIT. What is left between those lines and EBIT is shown as one
# residual, so that the uses of revenue add up to revenue.
#
# Net debt is the financial liabilities less cash. voestalpine tags its
# borrowings and lease liabilities as other financial liabilities, current
# and non-current; another issuer may tag them as borrowings, and the
# concepts above are then the ones to change. No issuer tags a net debt of
# its own: the figure a report states in its management report is usually
# defined more widely, netting other financial assets against the debt as
# well, and is not comparable with the one here.
#
# EBITDA is not derived. Depreciation and amortisation are not a line of the
# statements under a concept of the IFRS taxonomy, and voestalpine does not
# tag them anywhere in its reports, so every indicator that would rest on
# EBITDA -- the margin, net debt to EBITDA, cash conversion -- is shown
# against EBIT or against the operating cash flow instead.
wide <- wide %>%
  mutate(
    year = fy_label(PERIODEND),
    days = as.numeric(PERIODEND - lag(PERIODEND)),

    # Income statement
    other_operating_net = gross_profit - coalesce(distribution_costs, 0) -
      coalesce(admin_expense, 0) + coalesce(other_income, 0) -
      coalesce(other_expense, 0) + coalesce(associates_result, 0) - ebit,
    opex_and_other = gross_profit - ebit,
    net_finance_result = coalesce(finance_income, 0) - coalesce(finance_costs, 0),

    # Balance sheet
    # Two residuals per side of the statement: the wider one is what is left
    # of a total once the lines a chart shows are taken off it, and the
    # narrower one what is left once the further lines of a table are taken
    # off as well. Each table and each chart uses the residual of the lines
    # it shows, so that nothing is counted twice.
    assets_rest_noncurrent = noncurrent_assets - coalesce(ppe, 0) -
      coalesce(goodwill, 0) - coalesce(intangibles, 0) -
      coalesce(equity_method, 0),
    assets_other_noncurrent = assets_rest_noncurrent -
      coalesce(financial_assets_noncurrent, 0) -
      coalesce(deferred_tax_assets, 0),
    assets_rest_current = current_assets - coalesce(inventories, 0) -
      coalesce(receivables, 0) - coalesce(cash, 0),
    assets_other_current = assets_rest_current -
      coalesce(financial_assets_current, 0),
    liabilities = assets - equity,
    financial_liabilities = coalesce(financial_liabilities_noncurrent, 0) +
      coalesce(financial_liabilities_current, 0),
    liabilities_rest_noncurrent = noncurrent_liabilities -
      coalesce(financial_liabilities_noncurrent, 0),
    liabilities_other_noncurrent = liabilities_rest_noncurrent -
      coalesce(employee_provisions, 0) -
      coalesce(deferred_tax_liabilities, 0),
    liabilities_rest_current = current_liabilities -
      coalesce(financial_liabilities_current, 0),
    liabilities_other_current = liabilities_rest_current -
      coalesce(payables, 0) - coalesce(current_provisions, 0) -
      coalesce(current_tax_liabilities, 0),
    net_debt = financial_liabilities - cash,
    net_debt_wide = financial_liabilities - coalesce(cash, 0) -
      coalesce(financial_assets_current, 0),
    capital_employed = assets - current_liabilities,
    invested_capital = equity + net_debt,
    working_capital = coalesce(inventories, 0) + coalesce(receivables, 0) -
      coalesce(payables, 0),
    net_current_assets = current_assets - current_liabilities,
    goodwill_and_intangibles = coalesce(goodwill, 0) + coalesce(intangibles, 0),

    # Cash flow
    free_cash_flow = operating_cash_flow + investing_cash_flow,
    free_cash_flow_after_capex = operating_cash_flow - capex,
    cash_tax_paid = taxes_paid,

    # Tax
    tax_rate = income_tax / profit_before_tax * 100,
    cash_tax_rate = taxes_paid / profit_before_tax * 100)

# The indicators. Those that put a flow of a year against a balance use the
# average of the balance at the start and at the end of the year, which the
# first year of the window takes from the year read behind it; that year is
# dropped afterwards. A ratio of two figures of which one is missing is
# missing, which leaves a gap in the tables rather than a wrong number.
avg <- function(x) (x + lag(x)) / 2

wide <- wide %>%
  mutate(
    # Growth
    revenue_growth = revenue / lag(revenue) * 100 - 100,
    gross_profit_growth = gross_profit / lag(gross_profit) * 100 - 100,
    ebit_growth = ebit / lag(ebit) * 100 - 100,
    profit_growth = profit_owners / lag(profit_owners) * 100 - 100,
    eps_growth = eps / lag(eps) * 100 - 100,
    assets_growth = assets / lag(assets) * 100 - 100,
    equity_growth = equity_owners / lag(equity_owners) * 100 - 100,

    # Margins
    gross_margin = gross_profit / revenue * 100,
    ebit_margin = ebit / revenue * 100,
    pretax_margin = profit_before_tax / revenue * 100,
    net_margin = profit / revenue * 100,
    net_margin_owners = profit_owners / revenue * 100,
    ocf_margin = operating_cash_flow / revenue * 100,
    fcf_margin = free_cash_flow / revenue * 100,

    # Cost structure, as a share of revenue
    cost_of_sales_ratio = cost_of_sales / revenue * 100,
    distribution_ratio = distribution_costs / revenue * 100,
    admin_ratio = admin_expense / revenue * 100,

    # Returns
    nopat = ebit * (1 - pmin(pmax(coalesce(tax_rate, NA) / 100, 0), 1)),
    roe = profit_owners / avg(equity_owners) * 100,
    roa = profit / avg(assets) * 100,
    roce = ebit / avg(capital_employed) * 100,
    roic = nopat / avg(invested_capital) * 100,
    rogic = ebit / avg(goodwill_and_intangibles + ppe + working_capital) * 100,

    # DuPont, on the result and the equity attributable to the owners
    asset_turnover = revenue / avg(assets),
    equity_multiplier = avg(assets) / avg(equity_owners),
    owners_share = profit_owners / profit,

    # Capital structure
    equity_ratio = equity / assets * 100,
    gearing = net_debt / equity * 100,
    debt_to_capital = net_debt / (net_debt + equity) * 100,
    liabilities_to_equity = liabilities / equity * 100,
    goodwill_to_equity = goodwill_and_intangibles / equity * 100,
    noncurrent_funding = (equity + noncurrent_liabilities) /
      noncurrent_assets * 100,

    # Debt service and liquidity
    interest_cover = ebit / finance_costs,
    net_interest_cover = ebit / (finance_costs - coalesce(finance_income, 0)),
    cash_interest_cover = operating_cash_flow / interest_paid,
    net_debt_to_ocf = net_debt / operating_cash_flow,
    net_debt_to_fcf = net_debt / free_cash_flow,
    current_ratio = current_assets / current_liabilities,
    quick_ratio = (current_assets - inventories) / current_liabilities,
    cash_ratio = cash / current_liabilities,

    # Working capital
    days_inventory = avg(inventories) / cost_of_sales * 365,
    days_receivables = avg(receivables) / revenue * 365,
    days_payables = avg(payables) / cost_of_sales * 365,
    cash_conversion_cycle = days_inventory + days_receivables - days_payables,
    working_capital_ratio = working_capital / revenue * 100,

    # Cash flow quality and capital expenditure
    ocf_to_ebit = operating_cash_flow / ebit * 100,
    fcf_to_profit = free_cash_flow / profit * 100,
    accruals = (profit - operating_cash_flow - investing_cash_flow) /
      avg(assets) * 100,
    capex_ratio = capex / revenue * 100,
    capex_to_ppe = capex / lag(ppe) * 100,
    capex_cover = operating_cash_flow / capex,

    # Per share. No issuer tags the number of its shares under a concept of
    # the taxonomy, so it is the result attributable to the owners over the
    # earnings per share: the weighted average number the issuer used itself.
    shares = profit_owners / eps,
    book_value_per_share = equity_owners / shares,
    ocf_per_share = operating_cash_flow / shares,
    fcf_per_share = free_cash_flow / shares,
    payout = dps / eps * 100,
    payout_cash = dividends_paid / profit_owners * 100,
    dividend_cover_fcf = free_cash_flow / dividends_paid,

    # Comprehensive income
    oci_to_profit = oci / profit * 100)

# Altman's Z''-score, the variant for an issuer whose shares are not valued
# in the figures: it replaces the market value of the equity in the original
# score with its book value, so that the score rests on the statements
# alone. Above 2.6 the score reads as a safe zone, below 1.1 as a distressed
# one; it was fitted on manufacturers and is read as a direction of travel
# rather than as a probability.
wide <- wide %>%
  mutate(
    z_wc = net_current_assets / assets,
    z_re = retained_earnings / assets,
    z_ebit = ebit / assets,
    z_equity = equity / liabilities,
    z_score = 3.25 + 6.56 * z_wc + 3.26 * z_re + 6.72 * z_ebit +
      1.05 * z_equity)

# Piotroski's F-score, nine tests of the statements of a year against those
# of the year before it, each worth one point. It was built to sort value
# portfolios and reads as a summary of the direction the statements point
# in, not as a rating.
wide <- wide %>%
  mutate(
    f_roa = as.integer(roa > 0),
    f_ocf = as.integer(operating_cash_flow > 0),
    f_roa_up = as.integer(roa > lag(roa)),
    f_accrual = as.integer(operating_cash_flow > profit),
    f_leverage = as.integer(financial_liabilities_noncurrent / assets <
                              lag(financial_liabilities_noncurrent / assets)),
    f_liquidity = as.integer(current_ratio > lag(current_ratio)),
    f_shares = as.integer(coalesce(issued_capital, 0) <=
                            coalesce(lag(issued_capital), 0)),
    f_margin = as.integer(gross_margin > lag(gross_margin)),
    f_turnover = as.integer(asset_turnover > lag(asset_turnover)))

f_keys <- c("f_roa", "f_ocf", "f_roa_up", "f_accrual", "f_leverage",
            "f_liquidity", "f_shares", "f_margin", "f_turnover")
wide$f_score <- rowSums(wide[f_keys], na.rm = FALSE)

# The year read behind the window is dropped now that the averages, the
# growth rates and the tests against the year before are in place. Where the
# repository holds no year behind the window, the first year shown has no
# average to put a flow against and its returns stay empty.
if (nrow(wide) > n_years) wide <- wide %>% slice_tail(n = n_years)

years <- wide$year
max_date <- max(wide$PERIODEND)
first_date <- min(wide$PERIODEND)
n_shown <- nrow(wide)
cur <- wide %>% slice_tail(n = 1) %>% as.list()
prv <- if (n_shown > 1) wide %>% slice(n_shown - 1) %>% as.list() else cur
```

```{r texts}
texts <- facts %>%
  filter(FILING == latest$FILING, !is.na(TEXT), is.na(DIMENSIONS)) %>%
  inner_join(tibble(key = names(text_concepts),
                    CONCEPT = unname(text_concepts)), by = "CONCEPT") %>%
  arrange(key, coalesce(LANG, "") != lang) %>%
  group_by(key) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  ungroup()

text_of <- function(key) {
  value <- texts$TEXT[texts$key == key]
  if (length(value) == 0) NA_character_ else gsub("\\s+", " ", value)
}

```{r formats}
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Writing numbers and words
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Numbers are written as the language of the factsheet writes them.
big_mark <- if (lang == "de") "." else ","
decimal_mark <- if (lang == "de") "," else "."

fmt <- function(x, digits = 0) {
  # A figure that rounds to nothing is written as nothing rather than as a
  # signed nothing: an amount of minus four hundred thousand is 0 in a
  # column of millions, not -0.
  x <- ifelse(!is.na(x) & abs(x) < 0.5 / 10^digits, 0, x)
  ifelse(is.na(x), "–",
         formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits, big.mark = big_mark,
                 decimal.mark = decimal_mark))
}

# A growth rate or a change carries its sign, so that a fall is visible
# without reading the column beside it.
fmt_signed <- function(x, digits = 1) {
  ifelse(is.na(x), "–",
         paste0(ifelse(x > 0, "+", ""),
                formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits, big.mark = big_mark,
                        decimal.mark = decimal_mark)))
}

# Translate a label: `tr("Revenue", "Umsatzerlöse")`.
tr <- function(en, de) if (lang == "de") de else en

# A caption wider than the figure is clipped rather than wrapped, so it is
# broken into lines once here.
wrap_caption <- function(text, width = 125) {
  paste(strwrap(text, width = width), collapse = "\n")
}

# The source line in the wording of the corporate design.
source_caption <- caption_corporate_design(
  source = tr("ESEF annual financial reports, filings.xbrl.org.",
             "ESEF-Finanzberichte, filings.xbrl.org."),
  last = format(max_date, tr("%d %b %Y", "%d.%m.%Y")),
  lang = lang)

amount_label <- tr(paste0(currency, " million"), paste0("Mio. ", currency))

# The x-axis of every chart has one break per financial year, named as the
# tables name it.
scale_x_years <- function(...) {
  scale_x_date(expand = c(.02, 0), breaks = wide$PERIODEND, labels = fy_label,
               ...)
}

# Escape what typst reads as its own syntax, for the text that goes into the
# raw blocks of the cover and of the running head.
typst_string <- function(x) {
  x <- gsub("\\\\", "\\\\\\\\", x)
  gsub("\"", "\\\\\"", x)
}
```

```{r lines}
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The tables: one function for every table of the factsheet
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Every table is one row per line of a statement or per indicator and one
# column per financial year. `spec` describes the lines:
#
#   key      the column of `wide` the line reads, or "" for a heading
#   en, de   the label
#   digits   the decimals shown
#   unit     "amount"  in millions of the currency, as the figures are held
#            "raw"     as held, for a per-share amount or a multiple
#            "pct"     a percentage, which the key already holds
#            "signed"  a percentage or a change, written with its sign
#            "days"    a number of days
#   sign     -1 for a line the statements deduct, which the taxonomy tags as
#            a positive amount: the table shows it as the deduction it is
#   style    "" for an ordinary line, "total" for a sum, "head" for a
#            heading, "sub" for a line indented below the one above it
#
# `mark` adds a dagger to a line whose figure was read from a concept of the
# issuer's own taxonomy, so that a reader can tell the two apart.
line_spec <- function(...) {
  spec <- tribble(...)
  if (!"sign" %in% names(spec)) spec$sign <- 1
  if (!"style" %in% names(spec)) spec$style <- ""
  spec
}

mark_of <- function(key) ifelse(vapply(key, is_extension, logical(1)),
                                "†", "")

format_line <- function(values, unit, digits) {
  switch(unit,
         amount = fmt(values / scale, digits),
         raw = fmt(values, digits),
         pct = fmt(values, digits),
         days = fmt(values, digits),
         signed = fmt_signed(values, digits),
         fmt(values, digits))
}

render_lines <- function(spec, data = wide, unit_header = NULL,
                         cagr = FALSE, change = FALSE) {
  label <- if (lang == "de") spec$de else spec$en
  out <- tibble(item = label)
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(data))) {
    column <- character(nrow(spec))
    for (j in seq_len(nrow(spec))) {
      if (spec$style[j] == "head" || !nzchar(spec$key[j])) {
        column[j] <- ""
      } else {
        value <- data[[spec$key[j]]][i] * spec$sign[j]
        column[j] <- format_line(value, spec$unit[j], spec$digits[j])
      }
    }
    out[[data$year[i]]] <- column
  }

  # The change on the year before and the growth over the window, which only
  # an amount and a per-share figure are shown with: the change of a ratio is
  # read off the ratios themselves.
  if (change) {
    out[[tr("Change, %", "Veränderung, %")]] <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(spec)), function(j) {
      if (!nzchar(spec$key[j]) || !spec$unit[j] %in% c("amount", "raw")) return("")
      v <- data[[spec$key[j]]]
      if (length(v) < 2 || is.na(v[length(v)]) || is.na(v[length(v) - 1]) ||
          v[length(v) - 1] == 0) return("–")
      fmt_signed((v[length(v)] / v[length(v) - 1] - 1) * 100, 1)
    }, character(1))
  }
  if (cagr) {
    n <- nrow(data)
    out[[tr("CAGR, %", "CAGR, %")]] <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(spec)), function(j) {
      if (!nzchar(spec$key[j]) || !spec$unit[j] %in% c("amount", "raw")) return("")
      v <- data[[spec$key[j]]]
      if (is.na(v[1]) || is.na(v[n]) || v[1] <= 0 || v[n] <= 0) return("–")
      fmt_signed(((v[n] / v[1])^(1 / (n - 1)) - 1) * 100, 1)
    }, character(1))
  }

  # The marks and the styles, which markdown carries into the table.
  marks <- mark_of(spec$key)
  out$item <- paste0(out$item, marks)
  out$item <- ifelse(spec$style == "sub", paste0(" ", out$item), out$item)
  bold <- spec$style %in% c("total", "head")
  for (column in names(out)) {
    out[[column]] <- ifelse(bold & nzchar(out[[column]]),
                            paste0("**", out[[column]], "**"), out[[column]])
  }

  header <- c(if (is.null(unit_header)) "" else unit_header, names(out)[-1])
  knitr::kable(out, col.names = header,
               align = paste0("l", strrep("r", ncol(out) - 1)))
}
```

```{r charts}
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The charts: one function for a stack, a group of bars and a set of lines
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Each takes the keys of `wide` to show and their labels, in the order they
# are to be read, and leaves the corporate design to the sourced script.
chart_data <- function(keys, labels, scale_by = scale, data = wide) {
  data %>%
    select(all_of(c("PERIODEND", keys))) %>%
    pivot_longer(-"PERIODEND", names_to = "var") %>%
    mutate(value = value / scale_by,
           var = factor(var, levels = keys, labels = wrap_labels(labels, 34)))
}

chart_stacked <- function(keys, labels, subtitle = amount_label,
                          scale_by = scale, ncol = 2, data = wide) {
  ggplot(chart_data(keys, labels, scale_by, data),
         aes(x = PERIODEND, y = value, fill = var)) +
    geom_col(width = 250) +
    geom_zeroline() +
    scale_x_years() +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) fmt(x)) +
    scale_fill_corporate_design() +
    labs(caption = wrap_caption(source_caption), subtitle = subtitle) +
    guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = ncol)) +
    theme_corporate_design(base_size = chart_base_size,
                           axis.title = element_blank())
}

chart_bars <- function(keys, labels, subtitle = amount_label,
                       scale_by = scale, digits = 0, ncol = 3, data = wide) {
  ggplot(chart_data(keys, labels, scale_by, data),
         aes(x = PERIODEND, y = value, fill = var)) +
    geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 260), width = 240) +
    geom_zeroline() +
    scale_x_years() +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) fmt(x, digits)) +
    scale_fill_corporate_design() +
    labs(caption = wrap_caption(source_caption), subtitle = subtitle) +
    guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = ncol)) +
    theme_corporate_design(base_size = chart_base_size,
                           axis.title = element_blank())
}

chart_lines <- function(keys, labels, subtitle = "%", scale_by = 1,
                        digits = 0, zero = TRUE, ncol = 3, data = wide) {
  g <- ggplot(chart_data(keys, labels, scale_by, data) %>% filter(!is.na(value)),
              aes(x = PERIODEND, y = value, colour = var)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = linewidth_corporate_design) +
    geom_point(size = 1.4) +
    scale_x_years() +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) fmt(x, digits)) +
    scale_colour_corporate_design() +
    labs(caption = wrap_caption(source_caption), subtitle = subtitle) +
    guides(colour = guide_legend(ncol = ncol)) +
    theme_corporate_design(base_size = chart_base_size,
                           axis.title = element_blank())
  if (zero) g <- g + geom_zeroline()
  g
}
```

```{r cover, results='asis'}
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The cover and the running head
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# The issuer and the period are read from the filings, so the cover is
# written as typst rather than set in the front matter. A value goes in as a
# typst string, which keeps a name with a hash or an underscore in it from
# being read as typst's own syntax.
ts <- function(x) {
  if (length(x) == 0 || is.na(x)) x <- "–"
  paste0("\"", typst_string(as.character(x)), "\"")
}

# A column of the cover: a label and a value per row.
typst_kv <- function(items) {
  rows <- vapply(seq_along(items), function(i) {
    paste0("  text(size: 7.5pt, fill: soft, ", ts(names(items)[i]), "),\n",
           "  text(size: 8.5pt, ", ts(items[[i]]), "),")
  }, character(1))
  paste0("#grid(columns: (3.3cm, 1fr), row-gutter: 5.5pt, column-gutter: 6pt,\n",
         paste(rows, collapse = "\n"), "\n)")
}

period_range <- paste0(years[1], " – ", years[n_shown])

identity_items <- list()
identity_items[[tr("Legal entity identifier", "Rechtsträgerkennung")]] <- lei
identity_items[[tr("Legal form", "Rechtsform")]] <- text_of("legal_form")
identity_items[[tr("Domicile", "Sitz")]] <-
  coalesce(text_of("domicile"), text_of("address"))
identity_items[[tr("Reporting currency", "Berichtswährung")]] <- currency
identity_items[[tr("Financial years", "Geschäftsjahre")]] <- period_range
identity_items[[tr("Latest period end", "Letzter Stichtag")]] <-
  format(max_date, tr("%d %B %Y", "%d.%m.%Y"))
identity_items[[tr("Language of the report", "Sprache des Berichts")]] <-
  coalesce(latest$LANG, "–")
identity_items[[tr("Filings read", "Gelesene Einreichungen")]] <-
  as.character(nrow(filings))

summary_items <- list()
summary_items[[tr("Revenue", "Umsatzerlöse")]] <-
  paste(fmt(cur$revenue / scale), amount_label)
summary_items[[tr("Operating result", "Betriebsergebnis")]] <-
  paste(fmt(cur$ebit / scale), amount_label)
summary_items[[tr("EBIT margin", "EBIT-Marge")]] <- paste0(fmt(cur$ebit_margin, 1), " %")
summary_items[[tr("Profit for the year", "Jahresergebnis")]] <-
  paste(fmt(cur$profit / scale), amount_label)
summary_items[[tr("Earnings per share", "Ergebnis je Aktie")]] <-
  paste(fmt(cur$eps, 2), currency)
summary_items[[tr("Operating cash flow", "Operativer Cashflow")]] <-
  paste(fmt(cur$operating_cash_flow / scale), amount_label)
summary_items[[tr("Net debt", "Nettofinanzverschuldung")]] <-
  paste(fmt(cur$net_debt / scale), amount_label)
summary_items[[tr("Equity to total assets", "Eigenkapitalquote")]] <-
  paste0(fmt(cur$equity_ratio, 1), " %")

notice <- tr(
  paste("Compiled from the issuer's own annual financial reports as tagged",
        "in Inline XBRL and published by filings.xbrl.org. Every figure is",
        "a fact of a report or is derived from facts of the same report; no",
        "market data, estimate or forecast is used. The indicators are",
        "computed by this factsheet and are not the issuer's own key",
        "performance indicators, which a report defines in its management",
        "report and often defines differently. This is a summary of",
        "published accounts, not investment advice."),
  paste("Erstellt aus den Finanzberichten des Emittenten, wie sie in Inline",
        "XBRL ausgezeichnet und von filings.xbrl.org veröffentlicht",
        "wurden. Jede Zahl ist ein Fakt eines Berichts oder wird aus Fakten",
        "desselben Berichts abgeleitet; es werden keine Marktdaten,",
        "Schätzungen oder Prognosen verwendet. Die Kennzahlen werden",
        "von diesem Factsheet berechnet und sind nicht die Kennzahlen des",
        "Emittenten, die ein Bericht im Lagebericht definiert und oft",
        "anders definiert. Dies ist eine Zusammenfassung",
        "veröffentlichter Abschlüsse und keine Anlageberatung."))

cat("```{=typst}\n")
cat("#set page(numbering: none)\n")
cat("#let ink = rgb(\"#22282E\")\n")
cat("#let soft = rgb(\"#5C666F\")\n")
cat("#let rule = rgb(\"#DCE1E5\")\n")
cat("#let accent = rgb(\"#C10016\")\n\n")

cat("#v(1.4cm)\n")
cat("#text(size: 8pt, tracking: 1.6pt, fill: soft, ",
    ts(toupper(tr("Company factsheet", "Unternehmens-Factsheet"))), ")\n", sep = "")
cat("#v(4pt)\n#line(length: 100%, stroke: 1.2pt + accent)\n#v(14pt)\n")
cat("#text(size: 25pt, weight: \"bold\", ", ts(issuer_name), ")\n", sep = "")
cat("#v(3pt)\n")
cat("#text(size: 10.5pt, fill: soft, ",
    ts(tr("Annual financial reports in the European Single Electronic Format",
          "Finanzberichte im European Single Electronic Format")), ")\n", sep = "")
cat("#v(28pt)\n")
cat("#grid(columns: (1fr, 1fr), column-gutter: 16pt,\n")
cat("  [#text(size: 8pt, weight: \"bold\", ",
    ts(tr("The issuer", "Der Emittent")), ")\n  #v(6pt)\n  ",
    typst_kv(identity_items), "],\n", sep = "")
cat("  [#text(size: 8pt, weight: \"bold\", ",
    ts(paste(tr("Financial year", "Geschäftsjahr"), years[n_shown])),
    ")\n  #v(6pt)\n  ", typst_kv(summary_items), "]\n)\n", sep = "")
cat("#v(1fr)\n#line(length: 100%, stroke: 0.5pt + rule)\n#v(6pt)\n")
cat("#text(size: 7pt, fill: soft, ", ts(notice), ")\n", sep = "")
cat("#v(8pt)\n")
cat("#text(size: 7pt, fill: soft, ",
    ts(paste0(tr("Compiled on ", "Erstellt am "),
              format(Sys.Date(), tr("%d %B %Y", "%d.%m.%Y")), ". ",
              tr("Source: filings.xbrl.org, XBRL International.",
                 "Quelle: filings.xbrl.org, XBRL International."))),
    ")\n", sep = "")

# From here on every page carries the issuer and the period in its head and
# its number in its foot.
cat("\n#set page(\n")
cat("  header: [#set text(size: 7pt, fill: soft)\n",
    "    #grid(columns: (1fr, auto), ",
    "[#text(weight: \"bold\", ", ts(issuer_name), ") #h(6pt) ",
    "#text(", ts(paste(tr("Company factsheet", "Unternehmens-Factsheet"),
                       "·", period_range)), ")], ",
    "[#text(", ts(tr("ESEF annual report data", "ESEF-Berichtsdaten")), ")])\n",
    "    #v(-4pt) #line(length: 100%, stroke: 0.5pt + rule)],\n", sep = "")
cat("  footer: [#set text(size: 7pt, fill: soft)\n",
    "    #line(length: 100%, stroke: 0.5pt + rule) #v(-2pt)\n",
    "    #grid(columns: (1fr, auto), ",
    "[#text(", ts(tr("Source: ESEF annual financial reports, filings.xbrl.org. Own calculations.",
                     "Quelle: ESEF-Finanzberichte, filings.xbrl.org. Eigene Berechnungen.")),
    ")], [#context counter(page).display()])],\n", sep = "")
cat("  numbering: \"1\",\n)\n")
cat("```\n")

           "auszeichnet: kein Aktienkurs und damit keine",
           "Bewertungskennzahl, keine Mitarbeiterzahl, kein",
           "Auftragsbestand und keine Aufteilung nach Segment oder Markt,",
           "sofern der Emittent die Zahlen seiner Segmentangabe nicht",
           "ausgezeichnet hat. Die Seite zur Abdeckung der Auszeichnungen",
           "nennt, wonach gesucht wurde und was nicht gefunden wurde.")))

cat(paste(basis, collapse = "\n\n"))
```

## `r tr("At a glance", "Auf einen Blick")`

```{r glance}
# The panel of the latest financial year against the one before it. A
# percentage changes by percentage points, an amount and a per-share figure
# by a percentage, and a multiple by its own difference, so each line says
# which it is.
panel <- tribble(
  ~key,                  ~en,                        ~de,                            ~unit,    ~digits,
  "revenue",             "Revenue",                  "Umsatzerlöse",            "amount", 0,
  "gross_profit",        "Gross profit",             "Bruttoergebnis",               "amount", 0,
  "ebit",                "Operating result (EBIT)",  "Betriebsergebnis (EBIT)",      "amount", 0,
  "profit",              "Profit for the year",      "Jahresergebnis",               "amount", 0,
  "profit_owners",       "Profit, owners of parent", "Ergebnis, Eigentümer",     "amount", 0,
  "eps",                 "Earnings per share",       "Ergebnis je Aktie",            "raw",    2,
  "operating_cash_flow", "Operating cash flow",      "Operativer Cashflow",          "amount", 0,
  "free_cash_flow",      "Free cash flow",           "Free Cashflow",                "amount", 0,
  "assets",              "Total assets",             "Bilanzsumme",                  "amount", 0,
  "equity",              "Equity",                   "Eigenkapital",                 "amount", 0,
  "net_debt",            "Net debt",                 "Nettofinanzverschuldung",      "amount", 0,
  "ebit_margin",         "EBIT margin",              "EBIT-Marge",                   "pct",    1,
  "roce",                "Return on capital employed", "Rendite eingesetztes Kapital", "pct", 1,
  "roe",                 "Return on equity",         "Eigenkapitalrendite",          "pct",    1,
  "equity_ratio",        "Equity to total assets",   "Eigenkapitalquote",            "pct",    1,
  "gearing",             "Net debt to equity",       "Nettoverschuldung zu Eigenkapital", "pct", 1
)

change_of <- function(key, unit) {
  now <- cur[[key]]
  before <- prv[[key]]
  if (is.na(now) || is.na(before)) return("–")
  if (unit == "pct") return(paste0(fmt_signed(now - before, 1), " pp"))
  if (before == 0) return("–")
  paste0(fmt_signed((now / before - 1) * 100, 1), " %")
}

temp <- panel %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    item = paste0(if (lang == "de") de else en, mark_of(key)),
    unit_shown = case_when(unit == "amount" ~ amount_label,
                           unit == "pct" ~ "%",
                           unit == "raw" ~ currency,
                           TRUE ~ ""),
    before_value = format_line(prv[[key]], unit, digits),
    latest_value = format_line(cur[[key]], unit, digits),
    delta = change_of(key, unit)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select("item", "unit_shown", "before_value", "latest_value", "delta")

knitr::kable(
  temp,
  col.names = c("", tr("Unit", "Einheit"), years[n_shown - 1], years[n_shown],
                tr("Change", "Veränderung")),
  align = "llrrr")
```

```{r income-statement}
# The income statement as the issuer presents it, by function. The lines the
# statement deducts carry sign = -1, because the taxonomy tags an expense as
# a positive amount; `other_operating_net` is what is left between the
# functional expenses and the operating result, so that the column adds up
# whatever else the issuer put there.
render_lines(line_spec(
  ~key,                  ~en,                               ~de,                                        ~unit,    ~digits, ~sign, ~style,

  "gross_profit",        "Gross profit",                    "Bruttoergebnis",                           "amount", 0,        1,    "total",
  "distribution_costs",  "Distribution costs",              "Vertriebskosten",                          "amount", 0,       -1,    "",
  "admin_expense",       "Administrative expenses",         "Verwaltungskosten",                        "amount", 0,       -1,    "",
  "other_income",        "Other operating income",          "Sonstige betriebliche Erträge",       "amount", 0,        1,    "",
  "other_expense",       "Other operating expenses",        "Sonstige betriebliche Aufwendungen",       "amount", 0,       -1,    "",
  "associates_result",   "Share of profit of associates",   "Ergebnis aus assoziierten Unternehmen",    "amount", 0,        1,    "",
  "other_operating_net", "Other, net",                      "Übriges, netto",                      "amount", 0,        1,    "",
  "ebit",                "Operating result (EBIT)",         "Betriebsergebnis (EBIT)",                  "amount", 0,        1,    "total",
  "finance_income",      "Finance income",                  "Finanzerträge",                       "amount", 0,        1,    "",
  "finance_costs",       "Finance costs",                   "Finanzaufwendungen",                       "amount", 0,       -1,    "",
  "profit_before_tax",   "Profit before tax",               "Ergebnis vor Steuern",                     "amount", 0,        1,    "total",
  "income_tax",          "Income tax expense",              "Steuern vom Einkommen",                    "amount", 0,       -1,    "",

  "profit_discontinued", "Profit, discontinued operations", "Ergebnis, nicht fortgeführte Aktivitäten", "amount", 0,   1,    "",

# a year of high prices beside a year of low ones.

  mutate(across(all_of(c("cost_of_sales", "gross_profit", "distribution_costs",

## `r tr("What revenue was spent on", "Wofür der Umsatz verwendet wurde")`

```{r uses-of-revenue}
# The parts add up to revenue: cost of sales and gross profit are revenue,
# and gross profit is spent on distribution and administration and on the
# other operating items, with EBIT left over. A year in which the other
# operating income exceeds the expenses has a negative bar for them, below
# the axis.
temp <- wide %>%
  mutate(other_operating_total = gross_profit - coalesce(distribution_costs, 0) -
           coalesce(admin_expense, 0) - ebit)

chart_stacked(
  c("cost_of_sales", "distribution_costs", "admin_expense",
    "other_operating_total", "ebit"),
  c(tr("Cost of sales", "Umsatzkosten"),
    tr("Distribution costs", "Vertriebskosten"),
    tr("Administrative expenses", "Verwaltungskosten"),
    tr("Other operating items, net", "Sonstige betriebliche Posten, netto"),
    tr("Operating result (EBIT)", "Betriebsergebnis (EBIT)")),
  data = temp)
```

```{r working-capital-table}
# The days are the average of the balance at the start and at the end of the
# year over the flow of that year. The receivables and the payables the
# taxonomy tags are trade and other, so the days are a little longer than
# the days of trade alone; the inventory and the payable days stand against
# the cost of sales, which is the closest the statements come to what was

## `r tr("Returns on capital", "Kapitalrenditen")`

```{r returns-table}
# A return puts the result of a year against the average of the capital at
# its start and its end. The return on invested capital puts the operating
# result after notional tax against the equity and the net debt; the
# notional tax is the effective rate of the year, held between nil and the
# whole result, so that a year with a tax credit does not lift the return
# above the operating result itself.
render_lines(line_spec(
  ~key,              ~en,                                      ~de,                                      ~unit, ~digits,
  "roe",             "Return on equity, owners of the parent", "Eigenkapitalrendite der Eigentümer", "pct", 1,

  "rogic",           "Operating result to operating assets",   "Betriebsergebnis zum operativen Vermögen", "pct", 1
), unit_header = "%")

### `r tr("Where the return on equity comes from", "Woher die Eigenkapitalrendite kommt")`

```{r dupont}
# The return on equity is the net margin times the turnover of the assets
# times the leverage of the balance sheet, each of which moves for reasons
# of its own: a return held up by leverage is not the return of a business
# that earns more on what it sells. The product uses the result
# attributable to the owners, so the share of the result that is theirs
# stands in the decomposition as well.
render_lines(line_spec(
  ~key,                ~en,                                         ~de,                                       ~unit, ~digits, ~sign, ~style,
  "net_margin_owners", "Profit of the owners to revenue",           "Ergebnis der Eigentümer zu Umsatz",  "pct", 2,        1,    "",
  "asset_turnover",    "Revenue to average total assets",           "Umsatz zur durchschnittlichen Bilanzsumme", "raw", 2,      1,    "",
  "equity_multiplier", "Average assets to average equity of owners", "Bilanzsumme zu Eigenkapital der Eigentümer", "raw", 2, 1,  "",
  "roe",               "Return on equity, owners of the parent",    "Eigenkapitalrendite der Eigentümer", "pct", 1,        1,    "total",
  "owners_share",      "Share of the profit that is the owners'",   "Anteil der Eigentümer am Ergebnis",  "raw", 2,        1,    ""
), unit_header = "")
```

## `r tr("Cash flow quality and capital expenditure", "Qualität des Cashflows und Investitionen")`

```{r cash-quality-table}
# Whether the result was earned in cash. The accruals are the result less
# the cash the business produced and invested, over the average total
# assets: a result that keeps running ahead of the cash is a result built on
# accruals, which tends to reverse. Free cash flow is the operating cash
# flow and the investing cash flow together, which is how this issuer
# defines it; the second measure deducts the capital expenditure alone and
# leaves the financial investments out.
render_lines(line_spec(
  ~key,                         ~en,                                       ~de,                                           ~unit,    ~digits, ~sign, ~style,
  "operating_cash_flow",        "Operating cash flow",                     "Operativer Cashflow",                         "amount", 0,        1,    "",
  "free_cash_flow",             "Free cash flow",                          "Free Cashflow",                               "amount", 0,        1,    "",
  "free_cash_flow_after_capex", "Operating cash flow less capital expenditure", "Operativer Cashflow abzüglich Investitionen", "amount", 0, 1, "",
  "ocf_to_ebit",                "Operating cash flow to EBIT, %",          "Operativer Cashflow zu EBIT, %",              "pct",    1,        1,    "",
  "ocf_margin",                 "Operating cash flow to revenue, %",       "Operativer Cashflow zu Umsatz, %",            "pct",    1,        1,    "",
  "fcf_margin",                 "Free cash flow to revenue, %",            "Free Cashflow zu Umsatz, %",                  "pct",    1,        1,    "",
  "fcf_to_profit",              "Free cash flow to profit, %",             "Free Cashflow zum Jahresergebnis, %",         "pct",    1,        1,    "",
  "accruals",                   "Accruals to average total assets, %",     "Periodenabgrenzungen zur Bilanzsumme, %",     "pct",    1,        1,    ""
), unit_header = amount_label, change = TRUE)

### `r tr("Equity by component", "Eigenkapital nach Bestandteilen")`

```{r equity-components, results='asis'}
# The one place where this factsheet reads the dimensions of the taxonomy.
# The statement of changes in equity tags its columns against the axis of
# the components of equity, so the equity at each year end can be split the
# way the issuer presents it. The members are named as the taxonomy names
# them, an issuer's own member included.
members <- facts %>%
  filter(CONCEPT == concepts[["equity"]], !is.na(VALUE), is.na(PRDSTART),
         PRDEND == PERIODEND, !is.na(DIMENSIONS),
         grepl("^ifrs-full:ComponentsOfEquityAxis=[^;]+$", DIMENSIONS)) %>%
  mutate(member = sub("^[^=]+=", "", DIMENSIONS),
         label = gsub("([a-z])([A-Z])", "\\1 \\2",
                      sub("Member$", "", sub("^[^:]+:", "", member)))) %>%
  distinct(PERIODEND, member, label, VALUE)

if (nrow(members) == 0) {
  cat(tr(paste("The statement of changes in equity of this issuer tags no",
               "figure against the axis of the components of equity, so the",
               "equity cannot be split here."),
         paste("Die Eigenkapitalveränderungsrechnung dieses Emittenten",
               "zeichnet keine Zahl gegen die Achse der",
               "Eigenkapitalbestandteile aus, sodass das Eigenkapital hier",
               "nicht aufgeteilt werden kann.")))
} else {
  order_of <- members %>%
    group_by(member, label) %>%
    summarise(size = max(abs(VALUE)), .groups = "drop") %>%
    arrange(desc(size))
  temp <- members %>%
    mutate(year = fy_label(PERIODEND),
           label = factor(label, levels = order_of$label)) %>%
    filter(year %in% years) %>%
    select("year", "label", "VALUE") %>%
    mutate(VALUE = fmt(VALUE / scale)) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = "year", values_from = "VALUE",
                values_fill = "–") %>%
    arrange(label) %>%
    rename(item = "label")
  knitr::kable(temp, col.names = c(amount_label, names(temp)[-1]),
               align = paste0("l", strrep("r", ncol(temp) - 1)))
}
```

             tr("Total comprehensive income", "Gesamtergebnis"),
             tr("Dividends paid", "Gezahlte Dividenden")),

## `r tr("Screening indicators", "Screening-Kennzahlen")`

```{r f-score}
# Piotroski's nine tests of the statements of a year against the year
# before: each is worth one point and the score is their sum. It was built
# to sort portfolios of cheap shares into the ones whose accounts were
# improving and the ones whose accounts were not, so it reads as a direction
# of travel rather than as a rating. A test whose figures are missing in
# either year leaves the score of that year empty rather than counting the
# test as failed.
score_rows <- tribble(
  ~key,          ~en,                                               ~de,
  "f_roa",       "Return on total assets above nil",                "Gesamtkapitalrendite über null",
  "f_ocf",       "Operating cash flow above nil",                   "Operativer Cashflow über null",
  "f_roa_up",    "Return on total assets higher than last year",    "Gesamtkapitalrendite höher als im Vorjahr",
  "f_accrual",   "Operating cash flow above the profit",            "Operativer Cashflow über dem Jahresergebnis",
  "f_leverage",  "Non-current financial liabilities to assets lower", "Langfristige Finanzverbindlichkeiten zur Bilanzsumme niedriger",
  "f_liquidity", "Current ratio higher than last year",             "Liquidität 3. Grades höher als im Vorjahr",
  "f_shares",    "Issued capital not increased",                    "Grundkapital nicht erhöht",
  "f_margin",    "Gross margin higher than last year",              "Bruttomarge höher als im Vorjahr",
  "f_turnover",  "Asset turnover higher than last year",            "Kapitalumschlag höher als im Vorjahr"
)

temp <- tibble(item = if (lang == "de") score_rows$de else score_rows$en)
for (i in seq_len(n_shown)) {
  temp[[years[i]]] <- vapply(score_rows$key, function(k) {
    v <- wide[[k]][i]
    if (is.na(v)) "–" else if (v == 1) "✔" else "✕"
  }, character(1))
}
total <- c(tr("**F-score, out of nine**", "**F-Score, von neun**"),
           paste0("**", ifelse(is.na(wide$f_score), "–",
                               as.character(wide$f_score)), "**"))
temp <- bind_rows(temp, as_tibble(setNames(as.list(total), names(temp))))
knitr::kable(temp, col.names = c("", years),
             align = paste0("l", strrep("c", n_shown)))
```

### `r tr("Distance to distress", "Abstand zur Insolvenz")`

```{r z-score}
# Altman's Z''-score, the variant whose fourth term takes the book value of
# the equity rather than its market value, so that the score rests on the
# statements alone. Above 2.6 the score reads as a safe zone and below 1.1
# as a distressed one, with the range between them undecided. It was fitted
# on manufacturers decades ago and is read here as a direction of travel.
render_lines(line_spec(
  ~key,       ~en,                                          ~de,                                              ~unit, ~digits, ~sign, ~style,
  "z_wc",     "Net current assets to total assets",         "Netto-Umlaufvermögen zur Bilanzsumme",      "raw", 3,        1,    "",
  "z_re",     "Retained earnings to total assets",          "Gewinnrücklagen zur Bilanzsumme",            "raw", 3,        1,    "",
  "z_ebit",   "Operating result to total assets",           "Betriebsergebnis zur Bilanzsumme",               "raw", 3,        1,    "",
  "z_equity", "Equity to liabilities",                      "Eigenkapital zu Schulden",                       "raw", 3,        1,    "",
  "z_score",  "Z''-score",                                  "Z''-Score",                                      "raw", 2,        1,    "total"
), unit_header = "")
```

```{r score-chart}
chart_lines(c("z_score", "f_score"),
            c(tr("Z''-score", "Z''-Score"),
              tr("F-score, out of nine", "F-Score, von neun")),
            subtitle = tr("Score", "Punktwert"), digits = 1, ncol = 2)
```

## `r tr("Coverage of the tags", "Abdeckung der Auszeichnungen")`

```{r coverage}
# How much of the report the factsheet could read. The share of the numeric
# facts tagged under a concept of the issuer's own taxonomy says how far the
# statements can be compared with another issuer's at all: a report that
# tags most of its lines with concepts of its own is a report whose figures
# only its own filings can be put beside.
coverage <- facts %>%
  filter(FILING %in% (filings %>%
                        filter(PERIODEND %in% wide$PERIODEND))$FILING,
         !is.na(VALUE)) %>%
  group_by(PERIODEND) %>%
  summarise(facts_numeric = n(),
            facts_dimensional = sum(!is.na(DIMENSIONS)),
            extension_share = mean(!startsWith(CONCEPT, "ifrs-full:")) * 100,
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(year = fy_label(PERIODEND))

found <- tibble(year = years) %>%
  left_join(coverage, by = "year") %>%
  mutate(keys_found = vapply(years, function(y) {
    row <- wide[wide$year == y, ]
    sum(!vapply(unique(keys_all), function(k) is.na(row[[k]][1]), logical(1)))
  }, integer(1)),
  keys_total = length(unique(keys_all)))

temp <- tibble(
  item = c(tr("Numeric facts in the report", "Numerische Fakten im Bericht"),
           tr("of which with dimensions", "davon mit Dimensionen"),
           tr("Facts under the issuer's own concepts, %",
              "Fakten unter eigenen Konzepten, %"),
           tr("Lines this factsheet looked for and found",
              "Von diesem Factsheet gesuchte und gefundene Zeilen")))
for (i in seq_len(n_shown)) {
  temp[[years[i]]] <- c(fmt(found$facts_numeric[i]),
                        fmt(found$facts_dimensional[i]),
                        fmt(found$extension_share[i], 1),
                        paste0(found$keys_found[i], " / ", found$keys_total[i]))
}
knitr::kable(temp, col.names = c("", years),
             align = paste0("l", strrep("r", n_shown)))
```

} else {

### `r tr("Lines looked for and not tagged", "Gesuchte und nicht ausgezeichnete Zeilen")`

```{r missing-lines, results='asis'}
missing <- vapply(unique(keys_all), function(k) all(is.na(wide[[k]])),
                  logical(1))
missing <- names(missing)[missing]

if (length(missing) == 0) {
  cat(tr("Every line the factsheet looks for was tagged in every year shown.",
         paste("Jede vom Factsheet gesuchte Zeile wurde in jedem gezeigten",
               "Jahr ausgezeichnet.")))
} else {
  temp <- lookup %>%
    filter(key %in% missing) %>%
    group_by(key) %>%
    summarise(concepts = paste(CONCEPT, collapse = ", "), .groups = "drop") %>%

               align = "ll")
}
```

### `r tr("Checks on the figures", "Prüfungen der Zahlen")`

```{r checks}
# The figures are the issuer's tags, as filed, and a tag can be wrong while
# the report a reader sees is right: the scale of a number is an attribute of
# the tag, invisible on the page. The checks put figures of the same report
# against one another, each of which the statements state as the sum of the
# others: total assets as the non-current and current assets, total equity
# and liabilities as the equity and the non-current and current liabilities,
# the two totals as one another, revenue as the cost of sales and the gross
# profit, the profit as the result before tax less the tax, and the
# comprehensive income as the profit and the other comprehensive income. A
# difference points at a tag to look at in the report before the figure is
# used.
#
# The flag is set before the figures are formatted, since it compares them.
# It is meant for a tag with the wrong scale or the wrong sign, and not for
# rounding, so it is set where a difference exceeds a thousandth of the
# total assets.
checks <- wide %>%
  mutate(diff_assets = assets - noncurrent_assets - current_assets,
         diff_liabilities = equity_and_liabilities - equity -
           noncurrent_liabilities - current_liabilities,
         diff_balance = assets - equity_and_liabilities,
         diff_revenue = revenue - cost_of_sales - gross_profit,
         profit_continuing_shown = coalesce(profit_continuing, profit),
         diff_profit = profit_continuing_shown - profit_before_tax + income_tax,
         diff_discontinued = profit - profit_continuing_shown -
           coalesce(profit_discontinued, 0),
         diff_owners = profit - profit_owners - profit_nci,
         diff_ci = comprehensive_income - profit - oci,
         diff_cash = cash_change - operating_cash_flow -
           investing_cash_flow - financing_cash_flow)

diff_keys <- c("diff_assets", "diff_liabilities", "diff_balance",
               "diff_revenue", "diff_profit", "diff_discontinued",
               "diff_owners", "diff_ci", "diff_cash")
checks$flag <- ifelse(
  apply(abs(as.matrix(checks[diff_keys])), 1, max, na.rm = TRUE) >
    checks$assets / 1000,
  tr("check", "prüfen"), "")

check_rows <- tribble(
  ~key,               ~en,                                                        ~de,
  "diff_assets",      "Total assets less non-current and current assets",          "Bilanzsumme abzüglich lang- und kurzfristiger Aktiva",
  "diff_liabilities", "Equity and liabilities less equity and the liabilities",    "Passiva abzüglich Eigenkapital und Schulden",
  "diff_balance",     "Total assets less total equity and liabilities",            "Aktiva abzüglich Passiva",
  "diff_revenue",     "Revenue less cost of sales and gross profit",               "Umsatz abzüglich Umsatzkosten und Bruttoergebnis",
  "diff_profit",      "Profit of the continuing operations less profit before tax plus the tax", "Ergebnis der fortgeführten Aktivitäten abzüglich Vorsteuerergebnis plus Steuern",
  "diff_discontinued", "Profit less the continuing and the discontinued operations", "Jahresergebnis abzüglich fortgeführter und nicht fortgeführter Aktivitäten",
  "diff_owners",      "Profit less the owners' and the non-controlling share",     "Jahresergebnis abzüglich Anteile",
  "diff_ci",          "Comprehensive income less profit and other comprehensive income", "Gesamtergebnis abzüglich Jahresergebnis und sonstiges Ergebnis",
  "diff_cash",        "Movement in cash less the three cash flows",                "Veränderung der Zahlungsmittel abzüglich der drei Cashflows"
)

temp <- tibble(item = if (lang == "de") check_rows$de else check_rows$en)
for (i in seq_len(n_shown)) {
  value <- unlist(checks[i, check_rows$key])
  # A difference of less than a hundredth of a million is a rounding of the
  # tag itself and is written as nil rather than as a signed nothing.
  value[!is.na(value) & abs(value) < scale / 100] <- 0
  temp[[years[i]]] <- fmt(value / scale, 1)
}
temp <- bind_rows(temp, as_tibble(setNames(
  as.list(c(tr("**Tag to look at**", "**Auszeichnung prüfen**"),
            ifelse(nzchar(checks$flag), paste0("**", checks$flag, "**"), ""))),
  names(temp))))
knitr::kable(temp, col.names = c(amount_label, years),
             align = paste0("l", strrep("r", n_shown)))
```

## `r tr("The filings behind the figures", "Die Einreichungen hinter den Zahlen")`

```{r filings-table}
# Every filing of the years shown, whether the figures were taken from it or
# not. An issuer may file the same report twice -- in two languages, or
# corrected -- and each filing is a row with facts of its own.
temp <- filings_all %>%
  filter(PERIODEND %in% wide$PERIODEND) %>%
  arrange(desc(PERIODEND), FILING) %>%
  transmute(FILING,
            PERIODEND = format(PERIODEND, "%Y-%m-%d"),
            LANG = coalesce(LANG, ""),
            used = ifelse(FILING %in% filings$FILING, "✔", ""),
            ERRORS = coalesce(ERRORS, 0L),
            WARNINGS = coalesce(WARNINGS, 0L),
            INCONSISTENCIES = coalesce(INCONSISTENCIES, 0L),
            PROCESSED = format(PROCESSED, "%Y-%m-%d"))

col_names <- c(tr("Filing", "Einreichung"), tr("Period end", "Stichtag"),
               tr("Language", "Sprache"), tr("Used", "Verwendet"),
               tr("Errors", "Fehler"), tr("Warnings", "Warnungen"),
               tr("Inconsistencies", "Inkonsistenzen"),
               tr("Processed", "Verarbeitet"))
knitr::kable(temp, col.names = col_names, align = "lllcrrrl")
```

### `r tr("What a figure rests on", "Worauf eine Zahl ruht")`

```{r definitions, results='asis'}
# The definitions of the indicators this factsheet computes. They are the
# ones used here and are not the issuer's own, which a report defines in its
# management report: an issuer's net financial debt, its gearing and its
# earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation are usually
# defined more widely than the statements alone allow.
definitions <- tribble(
  ~en,                                                                                                                           ~de,
  "**Net debt** -- the current and non-current financial liabilities the issuer tags, less its cash and cash equivalents.",       "**Nettofinanzverschuldung** -- die kurz- und langfristigen Finanzverbindlichkeiten des Emittenten abzüglich der Zahlungsmittel.",
  "**Capital employed** -- total assets less current liabilities. **Invested capital** -- total equity plus net debt.",           "**Eingesetztes Kapital** -- Bilanzsumme abzüglich kurzfristiger Schulden. **Investiertes Kapital** -- Eigenkapital plus Nettofinanzverschuldung.",
  "**Return on equity** -- the profit attributable to the owners of the parent over the average of the equity attributable to them at the start and at the end of the year.", "**Eigenkapitalrendite** -- Ergebnis der Eigentümer über dem Durchschnitt ihres Eigenkapitals zu Jahresbeginn und Jahresende.",
  "**Return on capital employed** -- the operating result over the average capital employed. **Return on invested capital** -- the operating result less notional tax at the effective rate of the year, over the average invested capital.", "**Rendite auf das eingesetzte Kapital** -- Betriebsergebnis über dem durchschnittlich eingesetzten Kapital. **Rendite auf das investierte Kapital** -- Betriebsergebnis nach kalkulatorischer Steuer über dem durchschnittlich investierten Kapital.",
  "**Working capital** -- inventories plus trade and other receivables less trade and other payables. The days of each put the average balance over the flow of the year, the inventory and the payable days over the cost of sales.", "**Working Capital** -- Vorräte plus Forderungen abzüglich Verbindlichkeiten. Die Tage setzen den durchschnittlichen Bestand zum Fluss des Jahres, Vorrats- und Verbindlichkeitendauer zu den Umsatzkosten.",
  "**Free cash flow** -- the cash flow from operating activities plus the cash flow from investing activities, which is how this issuer defines it: the investing flow carries the financial investments as well as the capital expenditure.", "**Free Cashflow** -- Cashflow aus der Betriebstätigkeit plus Cashflow aus der Investitionstätigkeit, wie dieser Emittent ihn definiert: der Investitionscashflow umfasst auch Finanzinvestitionen.",
  "**Accruals** -- the profit for the year less the operating and the investing cash flow, over the average total assets. The measure follows Sloan (1996): a result that runs ahead of the cash tends to reverse.", "**Periodenabgrenzungen** -- Jahresergebnis abzüglich operativem und Investitions-Cashflow, über der durchschnittlichen Bilanzsumme, nach Sloan (1996).",
  "**Weighted average number of shares** -- the profit attributable to the owners over the earnings per share the issuer states, since no issuer tags the number itself. **Book value per share** -- the equity attributable to the owners over that number.", "**Gewichtete Anzahl der Aktien** -- Ergebnis der Eigentümer über dem ausgewiesenen Ergebnis je Aktie, da kein Emittent die Anzahl selbst auszeichnet. **Buchwert je Aktie** -- Eigenkapital der Eigentümer über dieser Anzahl.",
  "**F-score** -- Piotroski (2000): nine tests of the statements of a year against the year before, each worth one point.",        "**F-Score** -- Piotroski (2000): neun Tests des Abschlusses gegen das Vorjahr, je ein Punkt.",
  "**Z''-score** -- Altman's variant for an issuer whose shares are not valued in the figures: 3.25 + 6.56 times net current assets, 3.26 times retained earnings and 6.72 times the operating result, each over total assets, plus 1.05 times equity over liabilities.", "**Z''-Score** -- Altmans Variante mit dem Buchwert des Eigenkapitals: 3,25 + 6,56 mal Netto-Umlaufvermögen, 3,26 mal Gewinnrücklagen und 6,72 mal Betriebsergebnis, je über der Bilanzsumme, plus 1,05 mal Eigenkapital zu Schulden.",
  "**A dagger (†)** -- the figure was read from a concept of the issuer's own taxonomy rather than from the IFRS taxonomy. **A dash (–)** -- the issuer did not tag the figure in that year, or a figure the indicator needs is missing.", "**Ein Kreuz (†)** -- die Zahl wurde aus einem eigenen Konzept des Emittenten gelesen. **Ein Strich (–)** -- der Emittent hat die Zahl in diesem Jahr nicht ausgezeichnet.")

cat(paste0("- ", if (lang == "de") definitions$de else definitions$en,
           collapse = "\n"))
```

         "is not complete: a filing with technical errors may have no ",

         "found for this issuer, and the validation counts are the ",
         "repository's own.\n\nThe figures were read into the data lake by ",
